titulo: Café and food: querer, quisiera, numbers to 100: Numbers from 20 to 100 and prices

aula.titulo: Café and food: querer, quisiera, numbers to 100
aula.objetivo: Order food and drink at a café or restaurant with «querer» and «quisiera», count from 20 to 100, say prices in euros, ask for the check, and avoid the false friends «exquisito», «vaso», «cena» and «cola».

blocos.titulo: Counting from 20 to 100 and saying prices
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: from 20 to 29, Spanish writes it as a single word: «veinte, veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, veinticuatro, veinticinco, veintiséis, veintisiete, veintiocho, veintinueve». Watch the accent marks in veintidós, veintitrés and veintiséis. STEP 2: the tens are: treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa, cien. STEP 3: from 31 to 99, write ten + «y» + unit, as three words: «treinta y uno», «cuarenta y cinco», «noventa y nueve». STEP 4: «uno» drops the «o» before a masculine noun and becomes «un»: «treinta y un euros»; before a feminine noun, it becomes «una»: «veintiuna personas». And «veintiuno» becomes «veintiún»: «veintiún euros». STEP 5: «cien» means one hundred. Before a noun, and when it's exactly 100, use «cien»: «cien euros». For 101 to 199, Spanish uses «ciento»: «ciento uno». STEP 6: to say prices in euros, Spain uses «euros» and «céntimos»: «Son tres euros con cincuenta» (€3.50). Say the decimal point as «con». STEP 7: useful questions: «¿Cuánto es?» (the total bill), «¿Cuánto cuesta?» (the price of one item) and «¿Cuánto cuestan?» (the price of several). STEP 8: the «c» and «z» are pronounced with a «th» sound (in Spain) in «cincuenta» (theen-KWEN-tah) and «cien» (thee-EN). In Latin America, that sound is an «s». STEP 9: to say the total naturally, use «Son…» plus the amount. Don't use «Es» with more than one euro: «Son tres euros».
blocos.comparacao: Spanish and English numbers work much the same way, but the writing differs. From 21 to 29, Spanish fuses everything into one word («veintiuno»); from 31 to 99, it's written as three words («treinta y uno») — like English «thirty-one», but with «y» (and) as a separate word instead of a hyphen. The small trap: never skip the «y» between the tens and the units.

erros.motivo: The «y» between the tens and the unit is missing.
From 21 to 29, the number is written as a single word.

blocos.enunciado: Say five prices out loud, in euros and céntimos, then read these numbers: 24, 37, 45, 58, 63, 71, 86, 92, 100. Ask for the check: «¿Cuánto es? — Son… euros con…»
Count from 0 to 20 out loud. Then say five orders using «quiero» and «quisiera».
